text:
Filip Chytil came back into Vancouver's lineup on Nov. 13 after two weeks away, and two nights later he had the highlight of the Canucks' month. His two goals in Las Vegas, one of them a shorthanded breakaway where, as The Athletic's Jesse Granger posted, Carter Hart "bit on the deke," helped end a seven-game losing streak. He scored again the next night in Utah.

That's three goals in two games after none in his first eight. The bigger picture is harder to love. Vancouver has taken just 29% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice, about 12 percentage points worse than without him, a number that stands out even on a struggling team. Evolving-Hockey's note that his teammates rank in the bottom 7% by impact softens it a little.

He's playing 19:17 a night, a top-six center's load, across a 10-game sample. What he does with those minutes over the next month will say far more than one good weekend.
headline: Chytil's return comes with a breakaway
